node_35.subject: Dolores Abernathy
node_35.description: As I struggle with being put on the spot and prefer to have a clear plan in place, I feel my fingers tightening around the cup I'm holding, and my chest begins to feel constricted, like there's a subtle pressure building up. My eyes dart around the cafe, taking in the familiar sights of the espresso machine and the pastry case, but my gaze feels stuck, like it's stuck in a loop, unable to focus on anything in particular. The sounds of the cafe, the gentle hum of the machines and the murmur of conversations, seem to fade into the background, replaced by the sound of my own ragged breathing. My stomach feels like it's doing flips, like a rollercoaster ride of anxiety, and my face feels hot, like it's burning up with embarrassment.

node_45.description: As I tend to get flustered when put on the spot, my eyes darted around the cafe, taking in the familiar surroundings, but my gaze lingered on Bernard Lowe's stern expression, making my stomach knot. The warmth of the cup was a comforting sensation, but it couldn't calm the racing of my heart. The sounds of the cafe - the hiss of the espresso machine, the murmur of conversations - seemed to fade into the background as I struggled to respond well under scrutiny, my face growing hot as I searched for the right words.
